problem_summary.summary: Insert one interval into an already sorted list of disjoint closed intervals, merging any overlaps while preserving order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: sorted, non-overlapping intervals and newInterval. Return the resulting interval array; modifying the input is not required.
constraints: intervals is sorted by start and contains no overlaps

brute_force.explanation: Copy the existing intervals plus the new one into a combined array, sort by start, and apply the standard merge scan.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Sorting restores the same ordering used by interval merging. Merging every closed interval whose start is at most the current end produces exactly the union while retaining sorted, disjoint output.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n log n) for sorting n + 1 intervals, followed by an O(n) merge scan.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) for the combined input and returned output.

optimized.explanation: Append intervals strictly before the new one, absorb every interval that overlaps its growing bounds, then append all intervals strictly after it.
optimized.correctness_idea: The input order means no sorting is needed. Before the first overlap, intervals cannot be affected; while starts are at most the growing end they join the merged interval; afterward all remaining intervals are disjoint and already ordered.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n), since each existing interval is inspected or copied once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) for the returned interval list; no sorting buffer is needed.

steps.condition: 5 <= 10, then [9,12] also starts <= the expanded end 10.
steps.action: Expand bounds first to [5,10], then to [5,12].

edge_cases.handling: The new interval is returned as the only interval.

edge_cases.case: New interval falls between existing intervals
edge_cases.handling: The prefix and suffix remain unchanged around the inserted interval.
Intervals touching the new interval are merged because overlap is inclusive.
